title: Sub-lemma C (necessity): F=0 implies lambda is a product on non-identical cells, via local-to-global gluing on the punctured grid

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Claim ($\Rightarrow$).** If $\mathbf F(\lambda_c Q^{(c)})=0$ then there exist $u,v,w,x\in(\mathbb R^*)^n$ with $\lambda_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}=u_\alpha v_\beta w_\gamma x_\delta$ on all non-identical cells.

**What must be proved.** (a) Vanishing of all the $2\times2$-minor-type relations of Sub-lemma A on the *punctured* index grid (diagonal/all-equal cells removed). (b) A local-to-global / connectivity argument: form a graph on indices whose edges are cells where a nonzero relation pins a ratio, show it is connected enough to glue local ratios into global factors. (c) The factors lie in $(\mathbb R^*)^n$ (no zeros) — derive nonvanishing propagation from the support hypothesis $\lambda_c\ne0$ on all non-identical $c$. (d) Removal of the diagonal must not break the gluing.

**Why hard.** Reconstruction from rank-one binomial relations on a grid with deletions; ensuring global consistency and nowhere-zero factors is the most delicate part of the theorem.
